title: Business Development Manager - Ethiopia
description: Are you GAME to JOIN US and be our new Business Development Manager? Soft Construct is on a search for a new player to join our team Responsibilities Identify and develop new business opportunities within the iGaming and gambling industry (platforms, casinos, betting solutions, and related products). Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, partners, and clients. Conduct market research and competitive analysis to identify trends, potential customers, and business expansion opportunities. Negotiate and close business deals to meet sales and revenue targets. Collaborate with the marketing and product teams to align business strategies and promotional activities. Attend industry events, expos, and networking conferences to expand the company’s presence and brand recognition worldwide. Monitor industry regulations and ensure compliance with local and international gaming laws. Prepare reports and presentations for management on business development progress and strategic plans. Carry out other duties assigned by the immediate supervisor, which are in line with the job description and do not contradict the labor code. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Marketing, IT, or a related field. At least 3 years of experience in business development, sales, or account management, preferably in the iGaming or gambling industry. Strong understanding of iGaming platforms, casino solutions, and gambling products is an advantage. Ability to conduct in-depth market research and competitive analysis. Knowledge of industry regulations and compliance requirements. Experience in developing partnerships and managing key accounts. Proficiency in CRM tools, business development software, and project management tools. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Result-driven and highly motivated. Ability to work independently and in a team-oriented environment. Persuasive with strong problem-solving abilities. Excellent negotiation and deal-closing skills. Knowledge of English language is required and knowledge of any additional language is an advantage. Open to travel for business meetings and industry events. Do you like to learn hard, work hard, and play hard? Do you imagine better things, technologies, future? If you answered ''Yes'' to at least two of these questions, then we might be a great fit for you.

title: Chief of Staff
description: Company Description Songo Design & Build PLC is a design-and-build company based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, offering an integrated approach that combines design, costing, and construction within a single contract and team. The company emphasizes accountability and clarity, providing one responsible party from the initial sketch through a twelve-month post-handover visit. Projects follow a structured, 21-stage program, each with a signed gate to document progress, quality, and decisions. Songo delivers finishing to shop-drawing standards, ensuring all materials and samples are approved before use, and manages the specification, sourcing, and clearance of imported finishing materials in-house. Guided by the ethos “Imagination, engineered,” the company values collaborative decision-making and thorough project execution. Role Description The Chief of Staff role at Songo Design & Build PLC is a full-time, on-site position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Chief of Staff will support the executive leadership by coordinating strategic initiatives, tracking key projects, and ensuring alignment between design, cost, and construction teams. This role involves structuring and facilitating leadership meetings, preparing briefings and reports, managing follow-ups on decisions, and maintaining clear communication across departments. The Chief of Staff will help improve internal processes, monitor performance against company milestones, and proactively identify risks or bottlenecks in the project pipeline. The role also includes building relationships with internal and external stakeholders, supporting resource planning, and acting as a trusted advisor to leadership to keep priorities on schedule and on budget. Qualifications Strong strategic planning, project management, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and deadlines. Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and collaboration skills to work effectively across design, engineering, construction, and finance teams. Analytical and problem-solving abilities, including experience with data-driven decision-making, performance tracking, and process improvement. Leadership and people-management capabilities, including facilitating meetings, guiding cross-functional work, and supporting change management. Experience in construction, architecture, engineering, or real estate development is highly beneficial; familiarity with design-and-build delivery models is a plus. Bachelor’s degree in business, management, engineering, architecture, or a related field; an advanced degree (e.g., MBA) is an advantage. High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism in handling confidential information and sensitive decisions. Comfort working on-site in Addis Ababa and engaging directly with project teams, clients, and partners. Experiance General experience : 6 years, 3 of them in a construction, engineering or property company Specific experience: At least 4 years as executive or personal assistant to a chief executive, general manager or director, preferably in construction, engineering or professional services Evidence required : Two references from executives served; a sample of minutes and a formatted letter; employment certificates with dates

title: General Manager – Ethiopia
description: Role Overview CIMC Tianda is seeking a locally based General Manager to lead its airport equipment installation and maintenance operations in Ethiopia. The successful candidate will take overall responsibility for the local team and airport service contracts, covering business performance, customer relations, installation management, operations and maintenance, HSE, personnel and subcontractor management. The position requires a hands-on manager who can maintain reliable airport operations while supporting the continued development of the local business. Key Responsibilities Assume overall responsibility for local business performance, including budgeting, profit and loss, cost control, cash flow and operating forecasts. Manage airport maintenance contracts, ensuring compliance with contractual requirements, SLAs and equipment availability targets. Manage airport equipment installation projects, including installation planning, site coordination, manpower arrangements, subcontractor management, progress control, quality, safety, testing, commissioning and handover. Oversee preventive and corrective maintenance, 24/7 breakdown response, spare parts, maintenance records and subcontractor performance. Maintain effective relationships with the airport, customers, government authorities and other local stakeholders. Support business development, contract renewals, quotations, variations, claims, invoicing and accounts receivable collection. Lead the local organization, including recruitment, shift arrangements, training, performance management and employee relations. Implement HSE and safety management systems, ensuring compliance with airport requirements and local regulations. Monitor contract profitability and implement measures to improve installation efficiency, operational performance and service quality. Submit regular business, financial and operational reports in English to the Regional Director. Coordinate major commercial, technical, installation and personnel matters with the Regional Director and headquarters. Mandatory Requirements Must have held a middle-management or above position at Addis Ababa Bole International Airport. This must have been an actual employment role based at the airport, with responsibility for airport operations, ground handling, airport equipment or GSE maintenance, or on-site contracted services. Project supply, installation work or occasional contact with the airport as a customer does not meet this requirement. Proven experience managing operational teams, technicians, shifts and subcontractors. Working knowledge of airport operations, installation and maintenance management, service-level requirements and safety management. Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, operating costs and customer relationships. Able to lead business discussions and prepare management reports in English. Based in Addis Ababa or able to work there permanently, with the legal right to work in Ethiopia. Willing to remain available for major operational issues outside normal working hours. Preferred Qualifications Previous General Manager, Operations Director, Country Manager or equivalent experience. Experience with passenger boarding bridges, GSE or other electromechanical airport equipment. Experience in full P&L management, installation project management, contract negotiation, claims and collections. Familiarity with Ethiopian employment practices and airport stakeholder management. Application Please submit an English CV clearly stating the employer, job title, employment dates and responsibilities for the middle-management or above role held at Addis Ababa Bole International Airport. Please also indicate your notice period, earliest available start date and salary expectations.

title: Senior Manager-Inclusive Financial Ecosystems
description: About The Role This is an opportunity to lead MSC’s work in digital financial services, payments and agent networks in Ethiopia. The Senior Manager will work with banks, payment service providers, mobile money and agent network operators, the National Bank of Ethiopia, EthSwitch and development partners to expand access to financial services in underserved communities. The role combines technical leadership, hands-on project delivery and business development. The Senior Manager will lead consulting assignments that address practical challenges in cash-in and cash-out (CICO) operations, agent performance and access to financial services. The role also involves guiding project teams in translating research and field findings into recommendations that clients can implement and scale, mentoring MSC colleagues, and ensuring that project deliverables meet MSC’s quality standards. Alongside project delivery, the Senior Manager will help grow MSC’s work in Ethiopia and the wider region by identifying new opportunities, building client relationships, shaping proposals and contributing to pitches and presentations. Requirements Key Responsibilities Lead the design and delivery of consulting assignments in digital payments, agent banking, mobile financial services and financial inclusion in Ethiopia. Set the technical approach, define work plans and oversee delivery from initial assessment through implementation. Assess how financial services reach customers and advise clients on agent network design, agent recruitment and performance, liquidity management, and cash-in and cash-out (CICO) operations. Lead market assessments and field research to identify barriers to accessing and using digital financial services, particularly in rural and underserved communities. Use the findings to develop payment delivery models that partners can implement and expand. Analyze financial and transaction data, market trends and operational risks. Translate findings into practical recommendations, implementation plans, technical reports and client presentations. Oversee project timelines and deliverables, review technical outputs and ensure that assignments meet client expectations and MSC’s quality standards. Build and maintain relationships with banks, payment service providers, mobile money operators, agent network operators, the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), EthSwitch and development partners. Lead client meetings, consultations and workshops to agree on priorities, validate findings and resolve issues that affect project delivery. Advise clients on how regulatory requirements, market conditions and operational constraints affect the design and rollout of digital financial services. Identify consulting opportunities in Ethiopia and the wider region. Build relationships with prospective clients and partners, shape proposals and technical approaches, and contribute to pitches and presentations. Mentor MSC colleagues through regular guidance, feedback and review of technical work. Share lessons and tools from assignments to strengthen delivery across teams. Qualifications/Requirements 14–15 years of relevant professional experience in digital financial services, digital payments, agent banking, mobile money, financial inclusion or management consulting in these areas, including experience leading technical assignments. A master’s degree in Economics, Public Administration, Business Administration, Social Sciences or a related discipline. Professional certification in digital finance, payments, financial inclusion or a related field Practical expertise in financial distribution networks, including agent network design and management, agent performance, liquidity management and CICO services. Demonstrated ability to assess how market conditions affect the adoption and expansion of these services. Strong understanding of Ethiopia’s financial services ecosystem, including the roles of regulators, banks, payment service providers, mobile money operators and payment infrastructure providers. Knowledge of regulatory frameworks for digital payments, agent banking and mobile financial services, particularly in Ethiopia. Familiarity with data protection requirements, including GDPR where relevant to client assignments. Strong analytical skills, including the ability to interpret financial and transaction data, assess market trends and operational risks, and use the evidence to guide decisions and recommendations. Proven consulting and project management experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams, managing work plans and deliverables, engaging senior stakeholders and maintaining client relationships. Business development experience, including identifying opportunities, developing proposals and presenting technical solutions to prospective clients and partners. Familiarity with emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and blockchain, and the ability to assess where they could address practical challenge

title: Midwife
organization: Madda walabu University Goba Refferal Hospital
description: Company Description Madda Walabu University Goba Referral Hospital is a teaching and referral facility that provides comprehensive healthcare services to the surrounding community. The hospital supports a wide range of clinical departments, with a strong focus on maternal, newborn, and reproductive health. As a university-affiliated hospital, it offers opportunities for professional growth, training, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams. The environment encourages evidence-based practice, continuous learning, and quality improvement in patient care. Midwives at the hospital play a central role in promoting safe childbirth and family-centered care. Role Description The Midwife is a full-time, on-site role based at Madda Walabu University Goba Referral Hospital in Adis Zemen. The midwife will provide compassionate, evidence-based care throughout pregnancy, labor, childbirth, and the postpartum period, including monitoring maternal and fetal well-being, assisting with deliveries, and managing routine obstetric cases. Responsibilities include counseling individuals and families on birth preparation, breastfeeding, and newborn care; recognizing and promptly referring high-risk cases; administering appropriate medications and interventions; and maintaining accurate clinical documentation. The midwife will collaborate with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to ensure safe, respectful, and culturally sensitive care. Additional duties may include participating in health education activities, mentoring students, and contributing to quality improvement initiatives within the maternity unit. Qualifications Clinical expertise in maternity care, including antenatal, intrapartum, and postpartum services. Strong midwifery skills covering pregnancy assessment, labor support, and childbirth management. Knowledge of childbirth processes and ability to support safe, respectful, and person-centered birth experiences. Foundational understanding of medicine relevant to maternal and newborn health, including basic emergency obstetric and neonatal care. Competence in lactation support, including breastfeeding counseling and early newborn feeding guidance. Recognized diploma or degree in Midwifery from an accredited institution; valid professional license or registration as required by local regulations. Previous experience in a hospital or maternity ward setting is highly desirable, especially in referral or teaching hospitals. Ability to work in multidisciplinary teams, communicate clearly with patients and colleagues, and maintain accurate medical records. Commitment to ethical, non-discriminatory, and culturally sensitive care, with strong empathy and resilience in high-pressure environments. Willingness to work shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays, as needed to ensure continuous patient care.

title: Assistant
organization: Dire Dawa Trade, Industry & INVESTMENT BUREAU
description: Company Description Dire Dawa Trade, Industry & Investment Bureau is a public sector institution responsible for supporting and regulating trade, industry, and investment activities in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia. The Bureau works closely with local and national stakeholders to create an enabling environment for businesses and investors. It focuses on promoting sustainable economic growth, improving service delivery, and ensuring compliance with relevant policies and regulations. Team members contribute to public service initiatives that directly impact local communities and the regional economy. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Assistant role based in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia. The Assistant will support daily administrative operations, including scheduling meetings, preparing documents, maintaining records, and handling correspondence with internal and external stakeholders. The role involves organizing files, entering and updating data, and assisting with the preparation of reports and presentations related to trade, industry, and investment activities. The Assistant may help coordinate events, workshops, or meetings, and ensure visitors and partners receive timely information and support. The position requires close collaboration with colleagues across departments to facilitate smooth office operations and efficient service delivery. Qualifications Strong administrative and organizational skills, including document management, scheduling, and record-keeping. Effective communication skills for professional correspondence, report assistance, and interaction with stakeholders. Basic computer proficiency, including use of office productivity software (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, email). Attention to detail and reliability in handling data, documentation, and routine office tasks. Ability to work collaboratively within a public sector environment and adapt to established procedures. Fluency in English and local languages commonly used in Dire Dawa is an advantage. Previous experience in an administrative or assistant role, preferably in government or office settings, is beneficial. Relevant diploma or degree in administration, business, or a related field is preferred.

title: Project Director – Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH)
description: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. PATH combines scientific and public health expertise, implementation experience, innovation, and strong partnerships with governments, communities, civil society, and development partners. In Ethiopia, PATH works closely with the Federal Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, health facilities, communities, local organizations, and development partners to strengthen health systems and expand access to high-quality, equitable health services. Project Overview The Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH) is a Gates Foundation-funded project that supports the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) and Ministry of Health (MoH) to develop a government-owned platform that systematically assesses country needs, prioritizes innovations, evaluates evidence and readiness, and supports the transition and scale-up of innovations within the Ethiopian health system. The IIH will establish an integrated approach across six innovation highways: Medical Devices Diagnostics Therapeutics, Family Planning and Nutrition Products Vaccines Technology, including digital health, artificial intelligence (AI), and biotechnology Bundled and Systems Innovations Phase 1 will focus on three tracer products across two highways: Medical Devices: AI-enabled Point-of-Care Ultrasound (AI-POCUS) Diagnostics: Near-Point-of-Care TB PlusLife and Ebola Diagnostics The project will work closely with the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, public health institutes, universities, innovators, development partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen innovation governance and develop practical pathways for evaluating, transitioning, and scaling priority health innovations. Position Summary The Project Director will provide overall strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the Integrated Innovation Highway project. The Project Director will be responsible for the design, planning, implementation, coordination, monitoring, and overall performance of the project. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to the IIH team and ensure that implementation is aligned with the Government of Ethiopia's priorities, Ministry of Health strategies, and Gates Foundation commitments. The Project Director will serve as a key point of contact for the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, Gates Foundation and other donors, grantees, technical partners, and other strategic stakeholders. A central responsibility will be to build and maintain strong relationships with government and ensure that the IIH contributes to a government-owned and sustainable innovation governance and transition-to-scale mechanism, rather than creating parallel systems. The Project Director will report to the PATH Ethiopia Country Director. Key Responsibilities Project Leadership and Management Lead the overall design, planning, implementation, coordination, and review of the IIH project. Develop and oversee annual workplans, implementation plans, budgets, milestones, and deliverables. Provide strategic and technical leadership to the IIH project team. Direct, supervise, mentor, and support project staff and direct reports. Ensure effective coordination across all project workstreams and implementing partners. Monitor project performance and ensure achievement of agreed results and donor commitments. Identify implementation risks, challenges, and bottlenecks and ensure timely corrective actions. Ensure compliance with PATH policies, donor requirements, government requirements, and project agreements. Promote adaptive management, innovation, learning, and continuous improvement. Ministry of Health and Government Engagement Serve as a senior project-level focal point between PATH and the Ministry of Health. Establish and maintain strong relationships with senior MoH officials and relevant directorates, particularly those working on Health Innovation, RMNCH, Quality Improvement and related health-system priorities. Support the Ministry of Health to lead and institutionalize the IIH approach. Facilitate strategic dialogue with MoH on health innovation priorities, evidence, evaluation, financing, transition, and scale. Ensure that IIH activities are aligned with national health strategies, policies, priorities, and systems. Support government-led decision-making and ownership of innovation assessment and transition processes. Facilitate coordination between the MoH, RHBs, public health institutes, universities, professional associations, development partners, innovators, and other relevant stakeholders. title: Owner
description: Company Description ALHILALI MINING EQUIPMENTS MANUFACTURING PLC is an industrial company focused on designing, producing, and supplying equipment for the mining sector. Based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the organization serves regional and potentially international clients in need of reliable mining machinery and related services. The company operates in a manufacturing environment that values safety, efficiency, and quality in all stages of production. Team members collaborate across engineering, operations, and business functions to support sustainable growth and long-term customer relationships. Role Description The Owner role at ALHILALI MINING EQUIPMENTS MANUFACTURING PLC is a full-time, on-site position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Owner oversees overall business operations, including strategic planning, financial management, and key decision-making for the manufacturing facility. Day-to-day tasks include setting company goals, monitoring production performance, ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory requirements, and managing relationships with suppliers, customers, and partners. The role involves directing management teams, approving budgets and investments, and guiding product development and market expansion initiatives. The Owner is also responsible for building a strong organizational culture, mentoring leadership staff, and ensuring that the company remains competitive and sustainable in the mining equipment industry. Qualifications Demonstrated experience in manufacturing, industrial operations, or mining-related businesses, with strong understanding of production processes and quality standards. Proven leadership and management skills, including the ability to set strategic direction, oversee teams, and make informed business decisions. Strong financial and business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, investment evaluation, and risk management. Ability to build and maintain professional relationships with clients, suppliers, regulatory bodies, and internal stakeholders. Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the capacity to represent the company in high-level discussions and partnerships. Knowledge of local regulations, safety standards, and compliance requirements relevant to manufacturing and mining equipment in Ethiopia. Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Engineering, Industrial Management, or a related field; equivalent practical experience may be considered. Track record of entrepreneurship or ownership in a similar sector is highly beneficial.

title: National Consultant -to support UN Women Ethiopia Country Office end line evaluation of the Project “Addressing the Effects of Conflict Related Sexual Violence in Ethiopia”
description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women Ethiopia prioritizes advancing gender equality and women’s empowerment by strengthening women’s leadership and participation, ending violence against women and girls (EVAWG), advancing Women, Peace and Security and gender-responsive humanitarian action, and promoting women’s economic empowerment and resilience as well as strengthening UN system-wide coordination and accountability for gender equality. Under its EVAWG portfolio, UN Women applies a comprehensive approach that encompasses prevention, strengthening laws and policies and the justice response, improving survivor-centered services, coordination, and strengthening data and evidence for policy and programming. Given the context in Ethiopia, particular emphasis is also placed on addressing Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (CRSV) and the needs of women and girls affected by conflict. This includes strengthening institutions and referral pathways to provide coordinated, survivor-centred services; improving access to health, psychosocial support, safe shelter, justice and legal aid; supporting survivors’ rehabilitation and economic empowerment; and strengthening coordination and evidence generation. Following the northern conflict in Ethiopia, women and girls have been subjected to various forms of violence and discrimination, which have negatively impacted their overall health and well-being. In response to this, and with the generous support of the Gates Foundation, UN Women, in collaboration with its implementing partners and key stakeholders, has been executing the project titled “Addressing the Effects of Conflict-Related Sexual Violence in Ethiopia.” The project has been implemented at the federal level, as well as in the Afar, Amhara, and Tigray regional states, since November 2023. UN Women has been collaborating with various institutions to implement the project, considering the partners' comparative advantages, the value they bring to the project, their expertise, and local presence. At the federal level, UN Women works closely with the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs (MoWSA). These two ministries oversee the overall implementation of the project and co-chair the project's steering committee at the federal level. Additionally, UN Women has partnered with the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) to ensure that the 8th Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey, particularly the Violence Against Women Module, is conducted with a gender-sensitive and survivor-centered approach through data collection and analysis. At the regional level, UN Women collaborates with various stakeholders. In the Amhara region, in addition to building the capacities of frontline service providers and establishing and strengthening coordination mechanisms, UN Women partners with two local civil society organizations—Association for Women Sanctuary and Development (AWSAD) and Agar Ethiopia Charitable Society. These partnerships focus on the establishment and expansion of two safe houses/shelters in Kombolcha and Bahir Dar that provide comprehensive services for survivors of violence. UN Women also partners with the Women Association of Tigray (WAT) to provide shelter services. Additionally, UN Women has signed a partnership agreement with the Afar Community Initiative for Sustainable Development Association (ACISDA) for interventions in the Afar region. The partners in all three regions implement a range of interventions, including community-level prevention and risk mitigation efforts, strengthening coordination, enhancing the capacity of service providers, facilitating women- and girls-friendly spaces, survivor rehabilitation and promoting economic empowerment for women and girls affected by the conflict. The overall goal of the project is 'Improved institutional commitment of government, civil society, and community where survivors of conflict related sexual violence and conflict affected women rehabilitated and reintegrated in the northern part of Ethiopia'. Outcome 1: Service providing institutions are responsive to provide survivor centred services Under this outcome, the project strengthens the systems, capacities, and mechanisms needed to provide coordinated, survivor-centred services for CRSV survivors.
